challenge.method: Compared GNU's Addendum with a hypothetical notice restricted to 1.1 that lists one Front-Cover Text and zero Invariant Sections. Then varied the feature list and version wording independently.
challenge.results: The single cover passage satisfies the feature condition. An otherwise identical notice designating nothing fails it. An unavailable notice leaves the condition unproved. Adding authorization for later versions changes the edition choice even with the same cover passage. GNU's sample cannot expand a single-edition authorization to 1.2, 1.3 or a draft.

limitations: The comment spells the identifier GFDL-1.1-only-invariants and also reverses the suffixes in its no-invariants alternative. The typed identifier supplies the canonical spelling.
GNU's Addendum illustrates a later-version grant. A work's actual authorized notice supplies its grant and designations and must be preserved separately from the unchanged license document.
